entries.name: Antikythera
entries.notes: Current Kokoro rendering verified correct: faster-whisper (small) transcribed the rendered narration as 'Antikythera' at 8.56–9.34s, and the opening 12s matched the script word-for-word. No respelling needed.

entries.name: Stais
entries.notes: MISPRONOUNCED in the 2026-11-15 render: Kokoro read the bare spelling as one syllable ('styes'/'skies', confirmed by faster-whisper small AND medium on the isolated 22–26.5s clip and the full pass). Target is the two-syllable Greek STAH-ees. IPA is the regular Modern Greek reading of the cited spelling Στάης (stress marked on ά, η = /i/); no standalone IPA/audio dictionary entry was located (checked Wikipedia, Wiktionary, Britannica, Dictionary.com, Forvo search 2026-11-15). kokoro_text 'Stah ees' was chosen empirically: Kokoro renders of it were transcribed by BOTH Whisper models as two syllables ('Star-Ease' / 'star ease'), i.e. /stɑː/ + /iː/. Caveat: the respelling voices the final consonant (/z/ rather than Greek /s/); 'Stah eess' was tested and heard as 'Star East', 'Stah iss' as 'star is' — both worse.
entries.source: Wikipedia 'Valerios Stais' — Greek spelling Βαλέριος Στάης; IPA derived from the regular Modern Greek reading of that spelling

entries.name: Valerios
entries.notes: Current Kokoro rendering heard as "Valerio's" by both Whisper models — recognisable and acceptable in English narration; no respelling applied. IPA is the regular Modern Greek reading of the cited spelling Βαλέριος; no standalone IPA/audio dictionary entry was located.

entries.name: Saros
entries.notes: Kokoro misaki G2P (British pipeline) already gives sˈɛːɹɒs — SAIR-oss. No respelling needed. Variant /ˈsærɒs/ (SAR-oss) exists; SAIR-oss is the lead form.

entries.name: Metonic
entries.notes: Kokoro misaki G2P (British pipeline) already gives mɛtˈɒnɪk — met-ON-ik, matching the cited stress. No respelling needed.

entries.name: Callippic
entries.notes: Kokoro misaki G2P has no entry for this word; no respelling has been empirically verified yet, so none is applied — the word is recorded here so future scripts use the verified pronunciation. Verify a kokoro_text with a render + transcription before adding one.

entries.name: Cleopatra
entries.notes: Standard English name; Kokoro renders it correctly. No respelling needed.

entries.name: Voynich
entries.notes: VERIFIED with a caveat: no standalone Wiktionary 'Voynich' IPA was found; the IPA here is the standard transcription consistent with Wikipedia's cited respelling 'VOY-nitch' and Wiktionary's 'Voynichese' /ˌvɔɪ.nɪˈtʃiːz/ (Voynich + -ese), plus the Polish cz = [tʃ] in Wilfrid Voynich's birth name Wojnicz. No respelling needed — the spelling is phonetic in English.

entries.name: muon
entries.notes: Standard English physics term; Kokoro renders it correctly. No respelling needed. UK IPA shown; US /ˈmju.ɑːn/.

entries.name: BCE
entries.notes: Initialism — spoken as letter names B-C-E. Kokoro misaki G2P already gives letter names (bˌiːsˌiːˈiː), and the 2026-11-15 render transcribed 'BCE' correctly at 32.86–33.36s. No respelling needed.
entries.source: Standard English initialism — letters spoken by name; Kokoro misaki G2P output (British pipeline) checked 2026-11-15

entries.name: Athens

entries.name: Exeligmos
entries.notes: Do NOT guess. Wiktionary has a definition only, no pronunciation section; the Wikipedia Antikythera mechanism article names the dial but gives no pronunciation. The only IPA found anywhere is HowToPronounce.com (crowd-sourced, malformed) — not a reliable source. Needs a classicist/linguist call before a respelling is recorded.

entries.notes: Do NOT guess. Checked Wikipedia, Perseus / Princeton Encyclopedia of Classical Sites, and the PATHs project page — all give the Greek Ταπόσιρις Μαγνὰ and history, none give any pronunciation. No Wiktionary entry exists.

entries.name: ScanPyramids
entries.notes: Do NOT guess. No pronunciation guide exists anywhere (checked the official site and HIP Institute / Cairo University press releases — the name is only ever written). It is a modern project brand name, transparently the two ordinary English words 'scan' + 'pyramids', but no source pronounces the compound as a unit, so it stays UNKNOWN.

confidence_scale.high: Dictionary / encyclopedia IPA (Wiktionary, Dictionary.com, Wikipedia) or the regular reading of a cited original-language spelling
confidence_scale.medium: Standard English words, or a respelling consistent with a cited source (e.g. Voynich from the cited respelling + Voynichese)
confidence_scale.unknown: No reliable evidence checked — flag for review, do not guess

entry_fields.aliases: Alternate spellings that map to this entry
entry_fields.ipa: IPA transcription, or null when status is unknown
entry_fields.kokoro_text: Text to feed Kokoro TTS instead of the raw name (mixed case so Kokoro does not shout), or null when the current Kokoro rendering is already correct or no respelling is empirically verified
entry_fields.name: Canonical display name, exactly as it appears in scripts
entry_fields.notes: Variants, caveats, or why this value was chosen
entry_fields.respelling: Human-readable respelling with CAPS on the stressed syllable (Serebii style), or null when unknown
entry_fields.ssml_phoneme: SSML <phoneme alphabet='ipa'> snippet, or null when unknown / not applicable. Kokoro SSML <phoneme> support is UNVERIFIED in this pipeline — kokoro_text is the primary route.

meta.rule: NEVER invent a pronunciation. If no reliable evidence exists for a name, its status is 'unknown — flag for review' with null IPA/respelling, NOT a guessed phonetic. Only verified entries with a non-null kokoro_text are applied to TTS input, and only at narration-generation time — the ledger, script text, and subtitles always keep the correct written forms.
